_comment: HOW TO ADD AN ARTICLE: Copy any article block below, fill in the fields, and run seed_kb.py. Re-running the script on an existing title will UPDATE it, not duplicate it.

_fields.title: Short, descriptive name for the article
_fields.content: Full article text. Use the Problem / Symptoms / Steps format for best LLM results.
_fields.department: null = visible to ALL departments. A string like 'finance' restricts to that dept only.
_fields.metadata: Optional free-form JSON for tags, category, severity. Can be left as {}.

title: VPN Connection Fails After Windows Update
content:
Problem: Cisco AnyConnect VPN fails to connect after a Windows OS update.

Symptoms:
- 'Unable to establish VPN' error on launch
- VPN worked correctly before the update
- Error code 429 or a blank VPN client window

Resolution Steps:
1. Press Win+R, type services.msc, and press Enter.
2. Find 'Cisco AnyConnect VPN Agent', right-click it, and select Restart.
3. Relaunch AnyConnect. If the error persists, proceed to step 4.
4. Uninstall AnyConnect from Control Panel > Programs.
5. Download the latest installer from the IT Software Portal (https://itportal.internal/vpn).
6. Reinstall and attempt to connect again.
7. If still failing, ensure UDP port 443 is not blocked by your local firewall.
8. If unresolved, raise a ticket with your machine hostname and the exact error message.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11
Category: Network / VPN

title: VPN Connected But Cannot Reach Internal Resources
content:
Problem: VPN shows as connected but internal websites, file shares, or services are unreachable.

Symptoms:
- AnyConnect shows 'Connected' status
- Internal URLs (e.g. intranet.internal) time out
- External internet works fine while on VPN
- Cannot ping internal servers by hostname

Resolution Steps:
1. Disconnect VPN and reconnect — sometimes the tunnel initialises with a stale route table.
2. Open Command Prompt and run: ipconfig /flushdns
3. Verify you are connected to the correct VPN profile (ask your IT team for the correct server address).
4. Check if split-tunnelling is the cause: try pinging 10.0.0.1 (or the known internal gateway). If it fails, the VPN tunnel itself is broken.
5. Disable any third-party firewall or antivirus temporarily and retest.
6. On macOS, go to System Preferences > Network > AnyConnect and remove, then re-add the VPN config.
7. If the issue persists only for specific internal apps, the app server may be down — check the IT status page.

Edge Case: If your machine clock is out of sync by more than 5 minutes, Kerberos authentication used by internal services will silently fail even if VPN is connected. Run: w32tm /resync in Command Prompt as Administrator.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11, macOS
Category: Network / VPN

title: Wi-Fi Not Connecting or Dropping Frequently
content:
Problem: Laptop cannot connect to the corporate Wi-Fi network, or the connection drops repeatedly.

Symptoms:
- 'Can't connect to this network' error on Windows
- Wi-Fi shows 'No Internet, Secured'
- Connection drops every few minutes
- Wi-Fi adapter shows as disabled or missing

Resolution Steps:
1. Forget the network and reconnect: Settings > Network & Internet > Wi-Fi > Manage Known Networks > Forget the corporate SSID, then reconnect.
2. Run the Windows network troubleshooter: Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Network Adapter.
3. Update the Wi-Fi driver: Device Manager > Network Adapters > right-click your Wi-Fi adapter > Update Driver.
4. Reset the network stack (run as Administrator in CMD):
   netsh winsock reset
   netsh int ip reset
   ipconfig /release
   ipconfig /flushdns
   ipconfig /renew
   Then restart your machine.
5. If the adapter is missing from Device Manager, the hardware may have failed. Try disabling and re-enabling it or perform a hard shutdown (hold power for 10 seconds).
6. If only the corporate SSID is affected, your device certificate may have expired — contact IT to re-enroll your device in MDM.

Edge Case: If you recently changed your Active Directory password, Windows may be caching old credentials for the 802.1x authentication. Go to Credential Manager > Windows Credentials and remove any entries for your corporate network.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11
Category: Network / Wi-Fi

title: Outlook Not Connecting or Email Not Syncing
content:
Problem: Microsoft Outlook fails to connect to the mail server, shows 'Disconnected', or stops syncing new emails.

Symptoms:
- Status bar shows 'Disconnected' or 'Trying to connect...'
- New emails are not appearing despite being visible in OWA (webmail)
- Outlook asks for password repeatedly
- Profile takes very long to load

Resolution Steps:
1. Check internet/VPN connectivity first — Outlook requires either direct internet or VPN for Exchange Online.
2. Click Send/Receive > Update Folder to force a manual sync.
3. If prompted for a password, enter your current corporate password. If it loops, clear cached credentials in Credential Manager (Control Panel > Credential Manager > Windows Credentials > remove any Microsoft/Office entries).
4. Restart Outlook in Safe Mode: press Win+R, type outlook /safe, press Enter. If it connects, a faulty add-in is the cause. Disable add-ins under File > Options > Add-ins.
5. If the profile is corrupt, create a new Outlook profile: Control Panel > Mail > Show Profiles > Add. Do not delete the old profile until the new one works.
6. For persistent disconnection on a domain machine, ensure the machine is not exceeding the Exchange ActiveSync device limit (IT Admin must remove old device registrations).

Edge Case: If Autodiscover is broken, Outlook cannot find the server settings. Run: outlook /cleanautocompletecache and also check that DNS resolves autodiscover.yourdomain.com correctly.

Affected Systems: Windows (Outlook 2016, 2019, Microsoft 365), macOS (Outlook for Mac)
Category: Software / Email

title: Microsoft Teams Audio or Video Not Working in Meetings
content:
Problem: Microphone, camera, or speakers are not functioning correctly in Microsoft Teams meetings.

Symptoms:
- Other participants cannot hear you
- Your camera shows a black screen or does not appear in the device list
- You cannot hear others despite audio being enabled
- Audio cuts in and out during calls

Resolution Steps:
1. In Teams, click your profile icon > Settings > Devices and verify the correct microphone, speaker, and camera are selected.
2. Run the test call: Settings > Devices > Make a test call.
3. Check OS-level permissions: Settings > Privacy > Microphone / Camera — ensure Teams is allowed.
4. Quit Teams fully (right-click tray icon > Quit) and relaunch.
5. Clear the Teams cache: close Teams, navigate to %AppData%\Microsoft\Teams and delete the contents of the Cache, GPUCache, and blob_storage folders. Relaunch Teams.
6. Update Teams to the latest version: Profile icon > Check for updates.
7. If using an external headset or webcam, unplug and replug the USB device. Try a different USB port.
8. Roll back or update the audio driver in Device Manager if the issue appeared after a Windows update.

Edge Case: In large meetings (100+ participants), Teams may automatically mute your microphone. Look for the 'You are muted' notification at the top of the screen. Also, if your machine is on battery-saving mode, the CPU throttling can cause video encoding to fail — switch to a plugged-in power plan.

Affected Systems: Windows, macOS
Category: Software / Collaboration

title: Laptop Won't Turn On or Fails to Boot
content:
Problem: Laptop does not power on, shows a black screen, or fails to complete the boot process.

Symptoms:
- Pressing power button produces no response
- Power LED is on but screen stays black
- Laptop beeps on startup (POST beep codes)
- Boot stops at the manufacturer logo or a spinning dots screen
- Blue screen immediately on boot

Resolution Steps:
1. Connect the charger and wait 5 minutes — battery may be fully drained.
2. Perform a hard reset: hold the power button for 15 seconds until the device shuts off, then press power once to restart.
3. If screen is black but power light is on: connect to an external monitor via HDMI to determine if the display is the issue.
4. Try a drain reset: remove the power cable, hold the power button for 30 seconds to discharge residual power, reconnect and power on.
5. If stuck at the logo screen: try booting into Safe Mode (hold Shift while clicking Restart, or press F8 on startup).
6. If beeping on startup: count the beeps and note the pattern. Common codes: 1 long + 2 short = GPU failure, 3 short = RAM issue. Report this to IT for hardware replacement.
7. If the laptop was recently updated and now fails to boot, boot from WinPE recovery media (IT team provides this) and run startup repair.

Edge Case: Bitlocker encryption can cause a boot loop if firmware (BIOS/UEFI) changes are detected (e.g., after a BIOS update). You will be prompted for a 48-digit Bitlocker recovery key. Retrieve this from https://aka.ms/myrecoverykey using another device and your corporate credentials.

Affected Systems: All laptop hardware
Category: Hardware / Boot

title: Blue Screen of Death (BSOD) Occurring Repeatedly
content:
Problem: Windows crashes with a Blue Screen of Death and an error code, either randomly or on specific actions.

Symptoms:
- System restarts unexpectedly with a blue screen
- Error codes such as IRQL_NOT_LESS_OR_EQUAL, MEMORY_MANAGEMENT, SYSTEM_SERVICE_EXCEPTION, or DRIVER_POWER_STATE_FAILURE
- PC freezes and then reboots

Resolution Steps:
1. Note the exact error code shown on the blue screen. It is visible for a few seconds or in the crash dump file.
2. Check crash dumps: open Event Viewer (Win+X > Event Viewer) > Windows Logs > System. Filter for 'Critical' events around the time of the crash.
3. Run Windows Memory Diagnostic: Win+R > mdsched.exe > Restart now. This tests RAM for errors.
4. Update all drivers, especially GPU and chipset drivers: Device Manager > right-click each major adapter > Update Driver.
5. Check for recent Windows Updates that may have caused the issue. Roll back if needed: Settings > Update & Security > View Update History > Uninstall Updates.
6. Run SFC and DISM to repair system files (as Administrator in CMD):
   sfc /scannow
   DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth
7. If BSODs are random and no pattern emerges, RAM or SSD hardware failure is likely. Submit a hardware ticket.

Edge Case: DRIVER_IRQL_NOT_LESS_OR_EQUAL after installing a new VPN, antivirus, or peripheral driver almost always points to an incompatible kernel-mode driver. Boot into Safe Mode, uninstall the recently added software, and retest.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11
Category: Hardware / System Stability

title: Laptop Running Hot or Overheating and Shutting Down
content:
Problem: Laptop surface is unusually hot, fan is extremely loud, or the machine shuts itself off due to thermal overheating.

Symptoms:
- Fan runs at maximum speed constantly
- Laptop bottom is too hot to touch
- System suddenly powers off without warning during intensive tasks
- Performance is very slow (thermal throttling)

Resolution Steps:
1. Ensure the laptop is on a hard flat surface, not on a bed or lap — fabric blocks the vents.
2. Check CPU usage: Ctrl+Shift+Esc > Task Manager. If a single process is consuming 90-100% CPU, end it.
3. Change the power plan: Settings > Power & Sleep > Additional Power Settings > select 'Balanced' instead of 'High Performance'.
4. Check if a background antivirus scan or Windows Update is running — these drive CPU and heat.
5. Use compressed air to blow dust out of the vents (do not open the laptop). This should be done by IT if under warranty.
6. Install HWInfo64 (from IT software portal) to monitor real-time CPU and GPU temperatures. Report readings to IT if CPU exceeds 95°C at idle.
7. If shutdowns are frequent, the thermal paste on the CPU may have dried out — this requires an IT hardware engineer to service.

Edge Case: Rapid battery drain combined with heat on a MacBook is often caused by a process called 'kernel_task' which Apple uses intentionally to protect the CPU. Ensure the USB-C charger port side is not too warm; a faulty cable can cause this.

Affected Systems: All laptops
Category: Hardware / Thermal

title: External Monitor Not Detected
content:
Problem: Laptop does not detect or display output to an external monitor or projector.

Symptoms:
- Monitor shows 'No Signal' or stays black
- Windows display settings shows only one display
- Laptop screen works fine but external does not
- Intermittent flicker on the external display

Resolution Steps:
1. Press Win+P and select 'Extend' or 'Duplicate' — Windows may simply not have been told to use the display.
2. Try pressing Win+Ctrl+Shift+B to reset the display driver without a full reboot.
3. Reseat the cable on both ends. Try a different HDMI or DisplayPort cable.
4. Try a different port on the laptop if available (e.g., switch from USB-C to HDMI).
5. Right-click Desktop > Display Settings > Scroll down > click 'Detect' under the Multiple Displays section.
6. Update the display/GPU driver: Device Manager > Display Adapters > Update Driver.
7. Test the monitor with a different device to confirm it is not a monitor hardware issue.
8. If using a docking station, try connecting the monitor directly to the laptop to isolate the dock as the issue.

Edge Case: On Windows 11, if the monitor uses DSC (Display Stream Compression) and your GPU driver is older, you may see a black screen. Updating the Intel/AMD/NVIDIA driver to the latest version resolves this.

Affected Systems: Windows, macOS
Category: Hardware / Display

title: Printer Not Found or Unable to Print
content:
Problem: User cannot find the office printer on the network or print jobs are stuck in the queue.

Symptoms:
- 'Printer not found' when trying to add a printer
- Print jobs stuck in the queue with status 'Error' or 'Deleting'
- Printer shown as offline despite being powered on
- Test page prints but jobs from specific apps do not

Resolution Steps:
1. Check that the printer is powered on and connected to the network (look for the network indicator light on the printer).
2. Clear the stuck print queue:
   - Open Run (Win+R) > type: services.msc
   - Stop the 'Print Spooler' service
   - Navigate to C:\Windows\System32\spool\PRINTERS and delete all files inside (not the folder itself)
   - Restart the Print Spooler service
3. Set the printer online: go to Devices and Printers > right-click the printer > See what's printing > Printer menu > uncheck 'Use Printer Offline'.
4. Remove and re-add the printer: Settings > Printers & Scanners > Remove the printer, then click 'Add a printer or scanner'.
5. If the printer does not appear in the scan, connect using its IP address: Add printer > 'The printer I want isn't listed' > 'Add a printer using an IP address or hostname'. Get the IP from the printer's front panel.
6. Update or reinstall the printer driver from the manufacturer's website.

Edge Case: After a domain password change, the printer share credentials stored in Windows may be stale. Go to Credential Manager > Windows Credentials and remove any credentials related to the print server (usually named with the server hostname).

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11
Category: Hardware / Printing

title: Keyboard or Mouse Not Responding
content:
Problem: Keyboard or mouse is unresponsive, partially working, or behaving erratically.

Symptoms:
- Mouse cursor does not move or is jumping erratically
- Keyboard keys not registering or outputting wrong characters
- Device worked previously and stopped suddenly
- Wireless device disconnects intermittently

Resolution Steps:
1. For wireless devices: check/replace the battery. Re-pair the device via the USB dongle (usually press a button on both the dongle and device simultaneously).
2. Try a different USB port. Avoid USB hubs — connect directly to the laptop or dock.
3. Test with a different keyboard/mouse to isolate whether it is a hardware or software issue.
4. Uninstall and reinstall the driver: Device Manager > Keyboards (or Mice and other pointing devices) > Uninstall device. Windows will auto-reinstall on reboot.
5. If specific keys are not working, check: Settings > Time & Language > Language > Keyboard. Ensure the correct keyboard layout is set (e.g., QWERTY vs AZERTY).
6. For touchpad issues on a laptop: check if a function key (e.g., Fn+F7) has accidentally disabled the touchpad.
7. If the keyboard types wrong characters: check that Num Lock and Scroll Lock are not interfering. Also disable sticky keys: Settings > Accessibility > Keyboard.

Edge Case: On macOS, if the keyboard stops working after a system update, resetting the SMC (System Management Controller) often resolves it. For Apple Silicon Macs, simply shut down, wait 30 seconds, and restart — SMC is reset automatically.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11, macOS
Category: Hardware / Peripherals

title: Webcam Not Working in Video Calls
content:
Problem: Laptop webcam or external USB camera is not detected or shows a black/frozen feed in video conferencing apps.

Symptoms:
- Camera shows as 'Not found' in Teams, Zoom, or Meet
- Camera shows a black or still/frozen image
- Camera works in one app but not another
- Yellow exclamation mark on the camera in Device Manager

Resolution Steps:
1. Check OS privacy permissions: Settings > Privacy & Security > Camera — ensure the conferencing app is allowed.
2. Confirm no other app is using the camera simultaneously (only one app can use the webcam at a time on Windows). Close all other video apps.
3. In Device Manager, check for a yellow warning icon on the camera. If present, right-click > Update Driver or right-click > Uninstall Device, then restart to reinstall.
4. For built-in cameras: some laptops have a physical privacy shutter or a function key (e.g., Fn+F10) that disables the camera — check for this.
5. For USB cameras: unplug and try a different USB port. Avoid USB 3.0 ports for older cameras as they can sometimes cause interference — try a USB 2.0 port.
6. Check the camera in Windows Camera app (search 'Camera' in Start). If it works there but not in Teams, clear Teams cache (%AppData%\Microsoft\Teams\Cache).

Edge Case: In Windows 11, third-party camera applications sometimes conflict with the Windows Camera Frame Server. If the camera shows as available in Device Manager but produces a black feed everywhere, go to Services (services.msc) and restart 'Windows Camera Frame Server'.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11, macOS
Category: Hardware / Camera

title: System Clock Out of Sync Causing Authentication Failures
content:
Problem: User cannot log into internal services, VPN, or domain resources, and the error message mentions time, clock, or Kerberos.

Symptoms:
- 'The time difference between the client and server is too great' error
- Kerberos authentication error when accessing internal apps
- Login works fine on the local machine but internal web apps reject credentials
- Issue appears after travelling across time zones with the laptop

Resolution Steps:
1. Check if your system clock matches real time: look at the clock in the taskbar. If it is off by more than a few minutes, this is the cause.
2. Sync the time immediately (as Administrator in Command Prompt):
   w32tm /resync /force
3. If the above command fails ('The service has not been started'):
   net start w32tm
   w32tm /resync /force
4. Ensure time is set automatically: Settings > Time & Language > Date & Time > enable 'Set time automatically' and 'Set time zone automatically'.
5. Reconnect to VPN and reattempt login.
6. On macOS: System Preferences > Date & Time > enable 'Set date and time automatically'.

Edge Case: If the machine is not domain-joined or cannot reach the domain's NTP server (time.internal), configure an external NTP server. Run as Administrator:
   w32tm /config /manualpeerlist:time.cloudflare.com /syncfromflags:manual /reliable:yes /update
   net stop w32tm && net start w32tm
   w32tm /resync

Affected Systems: Windows, macOS
Category: Software / Authentication

title: Account Locked Out or Forgot Password
content:
Problem: User's Active Directory / corporate account is locked out or they cannot remember their password.

Symptoms:
- 'Your account has been locked' message at Windows login
- Password reset email not arriving
- Able to log into some services but not others (partial lockout)
- Account locked immediately after resetting password

Resolution Steps:
1. Use the self-service password reset portal: https://passwordreset.internal (accessible without VPN).
2. Follow the MFA steps to verify your identity and set a new password.
3. After resetting, also update saved passwords in: Credential Manager (Windows), Keychain (macOS), and your email client to avoid repeated lockout from cached wrong credentials.
4. If self-service is unavailable, contact your manager to raise an urgent IT ticket with your full name and employee ID.
5. Repeated immediate re-lockout after password reset usually means an old device (phone, tablet) is still using the old password to sync email/VPN. Update credentials on all devices.

Edge Case: If your account locks out repeatedly within minutes of unlocking, search for background processes silently retrying with old credentials. Check: scheduled tasks, mapped network drives (run: net use), and any mobile device management profiles. One stale connection can trigger policy lockout within seconds.

Affected Systems: Windows, macOS, all SSO-connected services
Category: Access / Authentication

title: MFA (Multi-Factor Authentication) Not Working or Phone Lost
content:
Problem: User cannot complete MFA because the authenticator app is not generating codes, the phone is lost, or SMS codes are not arriving.

Symptoms:
- Authenticator app shows 'Account not found' or generates codes that are rejected
- SMS verification code never arrives
- Phone was lost, stolen, or replaced and MFA setup is lost
- 'Authentication failed' even with a correct code

Resolution Steps:
1. If authenticator codes are being rejected: ensure your phone's time is accurately synced (automatic time must be enabled in phone settings — TOTP codes are time-sensitive).
2. If SMS is not arriving: check mobile signal. Try requesting the code again after 60 seconds. Check that your registered number in your profile (https://myaccount.microsoft.com) is correct.
3. If you have a backup authentication method set up (email OTP, backup codes), use that to sign in and then re-register your MFA device.
4. If phone is lost or replaced and you have no backup method: you MUST contact IT directly (phone or in-person). MFA bypass requires identity verification. IT will temporarily disable MFA for your account for a 30-minute window so you can re-enroll.
5. To re-enroll MFA: go to https://aka.ms/mfasetup after IT resets your MFA registration.

Edge Case: If you are travelling internationally and SMS MFA codes are blocked by roaming, request IT to temporarily enable a backup method (email OTP or hardware token) before your trip.

Affected Systems: All — Microsoft 365, VPN, SSO
Category: Access / Authentication

title: Suspected Phishing Email Received
content:
Problem: User received an email that appears to be a phishing attempt — requesting credentials, payment, or containing suspicious links.

Symptoms:
- Email asking you to urgently click a link and log in
- Email from an external sender impersonating IT, HR, or a manager
- Unexpected password reset or invoice email you did not request
- Email contains a link to a domain that looks similar but not identical to a trusted domain (e.g., micros0ft.com)

Resolution Steps:
1. DO NOT click any links or download any attachments in the suspicious email.
2. DO NOT reply to the email or provide any information requested.
3. Report the email immediately using the 'Report Phishing' button in Outlook (available in the Home ribbon). This forwards it to the security team for analysis.
4. If the 'Report Phishing' button is unavailable, forward the email as an attachment to: security@yourdomain.com
5. If you already clicked a link or entered credentials: IMMEDIATELY change your corporate password and contact the IT Security team by phone. Do not wait.
6. The security team will investigate and notify you if further action (device scan, account reset) is required.

Edge Case: If you received the email via a personal email forwarding to your corporate mailbox, the phishing report button may not work correctly. In this case, forward the raw email headers to security@yourdomain.com.

IMPORTANT: IT will NEVER ask for your password via email. If you receive such a request, it is always a phishing attempt regardless of how official it looks.

Affected Systems: All — Email clients, Web browsers
Category: Security

title: Antivirus Alert or Malware Detected on Machine
content:
Problem: The corporate antivirus solution (e.g., CrowdStrike, Defender) has raised a threat alert on the user's machine.

Symptoms:
- A pop-up from CrowdStrike Falcon, Windows Defender, or similar showing a quarantined file
- Machine is running unusually slow with high disk or CPU usage
- Browser is redirecting to unexpected pages
- Files have been encrypted or renamed with a strange extension (potential ransomware)

Resolution Steps:
1. DO NOT dismiss or try to resolve antivirus alerts yourself. Note the exact threat name shown.
2. Disconnect the machine from the network immediately: unplug the ethernet cable AND disable Wi-Fi. If ransomware is suspected, also turn off the machine.
3. Contact the IT Security team IMMEDIATELY by phone: do not email (your email client may be compromised).
4. Do not attempt to log into any other accounts (email, banking) from this machine.
5. IT will remotely isolate the machine, collect forensic evidence, and begin remediation.
6. You will be issued a clean loaner device while your machine is imaged.

Edge Case: Sometimes corporate software deployments trigger false positives in antivirus tools (e.g., a new script deployed by IT is flagged as suspicious). If the alert appeared immediately after IT pushed an update, notify your IT team of the timing — they can whitelist the file. However, always treat alerts as genuine until IT confirms otherwise.

Affected Systems: All
Category: Security

title: Slow Computer Performance
content:
Problem: Computer is running significantly slower than usual — applications take a long time to launch, the system freezes, or tasks that used to be fast are now sluggish.

Symptoms:
- Programs take more than 30 seconds to open
- Mouse and keyboard input feel delayed
- 'Not Responding' shown in app title bars frequently
- Task Manager shows consistently high CPU, RAM, or Disk usage

Resolution Steps:
1. Open Task Manager (Ctrl+Shift+Esc) and click the CPU and Disk columns to sort by usage. Identify the process consuming the most resources.
2. Common culprits:
   - antivirus full scan — wait for it to complete
   - Windows Update downloading/installing — let it finish and restart
   - OneDrive syncing a large number of files — pause sync temporarily
3. Disable unnecessary startup programs: Task Manager > Startup tab > Disable anything not needed.
4. Check available disk space: if your C: drive has less than 10% free space, this causes significant slowdowns. Empty the Recycle Bin and run Disk Cleanup (search in Start).
5. Restart the machine if it has not been restarted in more than 7 days — memory leaks accumulate over time.
6. Check RAM: if you are running many applications simultaneously and have 8GB or less RAM, contact IT to discuss a RAM upgrade.
7. If the machine is over 4 years old and consistently slow, submit a hardware refresh request through the IT portal.

Edge Case: Slow performance specifically on HDDs (non-SSD machines) after a Windows update is often caused by Windows re-indexing the drive. Check: Windows Search indexing service in Task Manager. It will subside on its own within a few hours.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11
Category: Hardware / Performance

title: Unable to Install Software from IT Portal
content:
Problem: User is unable to install approved software from the corporate IT Software Portal, receiving errors or finding the portal inaccessible.

Symptoms:
- Software portal URL is unreachable
- Download completes but installation fails with a permissions error
- Installer prompts for an administrator password the user does not have
- Installation appears to succeed but the software does not appear

Resolution Steps:
1. Access the portal only while connected to VPN or on the corporate network.
2. If permission denied: standard employee accounts are non-admin. Software installation must be triggered from the portal itself — do not try to run installer .exe files directly, as these require admin rights.
3. If a portal-initiated install is failing, try logging out of the portal and back in, then retry.
4. Clear your browser cache and retry the portal — stale sessions can cause download errors.
5. If the software is critical for your work and the portal is not working, open an IT ticket specifying the software name, version, and business justification. IT can push it remotely via MDM.
6. Do NOT install software from external sources (manufacturer websites, download portals) without IT approval — this violates company policy and may trigger a security alert.

Edge Case: Some software requires a machine restart to complete installation and will show as 'installed' in the portal but won't appear until after a reboot. Always restart after a portal install if the app is not visible.

Affected Systems: Windows, macOS
Category: Software / Installation

title: SSL Certificate Error in Browser
content:
Problem: Browser shows a 'Your connection is not private', 'NET::ERR_CERT_AUTHORITY_INVALID', or similar SSL/TLS certificate warning when accessing internal company websites.

Symptoms:
- Red padlock or warning icon before the URL
- 'Your connection is not private' message
- Error code: NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID or ERR_CERT_AUTHORITY_INVALID
- Only occurs on internal .internal or company-specific domains

Resolution Steps:
1. Do NOT click 'Proceed anyway' for external sites. For known internal sites, you can proceed cautiously.
2. Check your system clock — an incorrect date/time causes all SSL certificates to appear invalid. Fix time sync first (see: 'System Clock Out of Sync' article).
3. For internal company URLs, this often means the corporate root CA certificate is not installed on your machine. This is automatically deployed to domain-joined machines. If your machine is not domain-joined, contact IT to install the corporate CA certificate bundle manually.
4. Try the page in an Incognito/Private window — if it works there, a browser extension is interfering. Disable extensions one by one.
5. Clear browser SSL cache: in Chrome, go to Settings > Privacy and security > Clear browsing data > check 'Cached images and files' and 'Cookies'.
6. If the error is for an external site (e.g., vendor portal), it may be a genuine expired certificate on their end — contact the vendor.

Edge Case: Corporate SSL inspection proxies (used by security tools like Zscaler or Netskope) re-sign all HTTPS traffic with a company certificate. If this proxy certificate is not in your trust store, ALL external HTTPS sites will show certificate errors. Ensure the Zscaler/Netskope root certificate is installed — IT pushes this via MDM, but it can get deleted.

Affected Systems: Windows, macOS — all browsers
Category: Network / Security

title: OneDrive Sync Errors or Conflicts
content:
Problem: OneDrive is reporting sync errors, showing files with a red X, or creating duplicate 'conflict' copies of files.

Symptoms:
- Files show a red X icon in File Explorer
- Notification saying 'OneDrive can't sync'
- Files named with '-username-PC conflict' suffix appearing
- OneDrive tray icon shows an exclamation mark

Resolution Steps:
1. Click the OneDrive tray icon and read the specific error message — it often tells you exactly which file and why.
2. Common error causes and fixes:
   - File path too long (over 260 characters): shorten folder names or move the file closer to the root
   - Invalid characters in filename (e.g., ?, *, :, <, >, |, "): rename the file removing these characters
   - File locked by another application: close all apps that might have the file open, then sync
   - File too large: OneDrive has a 250GB single-file limit
3. For conflict copies: open both the original and the conflict file, compare, keep the correct version, and delete the conflict copy.
4. Reset OneDrive sync: close OneDrive, open Run (Win+R) and type: %localappdata%\Microsoft\OneDrive\OneDrive.exe /reset — OneDrive will relaunch and re-sync.
5. If reset does not help, sign out of OneDrive (tray icon > Settings > Account > Unlink this PC), then sign back in.

Edge Case: If two people edit the same file simultaneously from different machines, OneDrive creates conflict copies automatically. This is by design. To prevent it, use real-time co-authoring in Office 365 apps (Word, Excel) which allows multiple simultaneous edits without conflicts.

Affected Systems: Windows, macOS
Category: Software / Microsoft 365

title: Payroll System Login Issues
content:
Problem: Employee is unable to log into the internal Payroll portal.

Symptoms:
- Password rejected despite being correct
- MFA prompt not arriving
- Account locked message on login
- Cannot access payslips or payroll history

Resolution Steps:
1. Attempt a self-service password reset at https://payroll.internal/reset using your corporate email.
2. If MFA is not arriving, ensure your registered phone number is correct under your profile settings on the payroll portal.
3. If account is locked, IT must unlock it — submit a ticket with your employee ID and your direct manager's name for verification.
4. Ensure you are connected to VPN before accessing the payroll portal (it is not accessible from the public internet).
5. Do NOT share payroll credentials under any circumstances. All access issues must be routed through IT.
6. Payroll portal access is provisioned by HR at onboarding — if you are a new joiner and have never had access, contact HR (not IT).

Edge Case: If you can log in but see incorrect salary figures or missing pay periods, this is a data issue and must be reported directly to the Payroll team (payroll@yourdomain.com), not IT. IT manages system access only, not payroll data.

Affected Systems: Payroll Portal
Category: Access / Authentication

title: New Employee IT Setup and Onboarding
content:
Problem: A new employee has joined and needs their IT environment set up — devices, accounts, email, and software access.

Symptoms:
- New joiner cannot log into their laptop
- Email account not created
- Missing access to required systems (Teams, SharePoint, etc.)
- Software needed for role not installed

Resolution Steps:
1. IT onboarding is triggered by HR. If accounts have not been created by the start date, HR must confirm the new hire request was submitted to IT at least 5 business days in advance.
2. Temporary first-login credentials are provided by IT in a sealed envelope or via the manager's corporate email.
3. On first login, the user will be prompted to set their own password and register MFA.
4. Standard software is pre-installed on the provisioned laptop via MDM. Any additional role-specific software must be requested through the IT portal with manager approval.
5. Teams and M365 access is automatically provisioned with the account. SharePoint site access must be granted by each site owner (usually the team lead).
6. If any access is missing after 48 hours of account creation, the new hire's manager should raise an IT ticket specifying which systems are needed and the business justification.

Edge Case: If a new employee joins urgently and there is no time for standard provisioning, IT can provide a temporary loaner device with a generic account scoped to required access only. This must be approved by a department head.

Affected Systems: All
Category: Onboarding / Access

title: Headset or Audio Not Working on Laptop
content:
Problem: Audio is not playing through headphones or speakers, or the microphone is not picking up sound.

Symptoms:
- No sound from speakers or headset despite volume being up
- Wrong audio device selected (e.g., playing through laptop speakers when headset is plugged in)
- Microphone is not picking up voice input
- Audio crackling or cutting out

Resolution Steps:
1. Click the speaker icon in the taskbar > click the arrow next to the volume slider to select the correct output device. Switch to your headset/speaker.
2. Check that the physical mute button on the headset is not engaged (many headsets have a hardware mute switch).
3. For USB headsets: unplug and replug into a different USB port. The device should auto-install.
4. For 3.5mm headsets: ensure it is plugged fully in. Use the combo jack (single port for both mic and headphones) and not two separate ports if your laptop only has one.
5. Update the audio driver: Device Manager > Sound, video and game controllers > Realtek Audio (or equivalent) > Update Driver.
6. Run the audio troubleshooter: Settings > System > Sound > Troubleshoot.
7. Set the default communication device: right-click the speaker icon in taskbar > Open Sound settings > Manage sound devices > set your headset as default for both Sound Output and Input.

Edge Case: Bluetooth headsets that lose pairing after a Windows update need to be removed and re-paired. Go to Settings > Bluetooth > click your device > Remove, then put the headset in pairing mode and reconnect. Also check that 'Hands-Free Telephony' service is enabled in Bluetooth device properties.

Affected Systems: Windows 10, Windows 11, macOS
Category: Hardware / Audio

title: GitHub Copilot License Not Active
content:
Problem: Engineering user cannot access GitHub Copilot in their IDE despite being assigned a license.

Symptoms:
- VS Code/IntelliJ shows 'Copilot is disabled or not authorized'
- GitHub settings show no active Copilot subscription
- Prompted to start a free trial

Resolution Steps:
1. Ensure you are signed into the IDE with your corporate GitHub account, not your personal one.
2. Go to github.com > Settings > Organizations and ensure you have authenticated via the corporate SSO.
3. In your IDE, sign out of the GitHub account and sign back in to force a token refresh.
4. If it still fails, the license provisioning sync might be delayed. Wait 1 hour after access was granted.
5. If the issue persists, raise an IT ticket specifically for 'Engineering Tools'.

Edge Case: If you are using a strictly blocked corporate VPN node, the IDE extension might fail to reach GitHub's telemetry servers. Try switching to a different VPN region.

Affected Systems: VS Code, JetBrains, Visual Studio
Category: Software / Engineering Tools

title: AWS Client VPN Authentication Fails
content:
Problem: Unable to connect to the AWS Client VPN to access internal engineering environments.

Symptoms:
- AWS VPN Client hangs on 'Connecting'
- 'Authentication failed' error after SAML login
- SAML browser window does not pop up

Resolution Steps:
1. Ensure you are using the latest AWS VPN Client from the software portal.
2. If the SAML browser window does not appear, change your default browser to Chrome or Edge and try again.
3. If authentication fails after logging in, your role may not have the required AWS SSO group assignment. Check with your Engineering Manager to ensure you are in the correct group.
4. Clear the AWS VPN Client cache: go to %AppData%\AWSVPNClient and delete the folder contents.
5. If still failing, check the engineering status page for AWS IAM outages.

Affected Systems: AWS VPN Client
Category: Network / AWS

title: Workday Performance Review Portal Access
content:
Problem: HR staff cannot access the administrator side of the Workday Performance Review portal.

Symptoms:
- Missing the 'Performance Management' tile in Workday
- 'Access Denied' when trying to view an employee's review
- Reports fail to generate due to missing permissions

Resolution Steps:
1. Workday administrator roles are separate from standard HR roles. Ensure you have the 'HR Business Partner - Admin' security group assigned.
2. If you recently changed roles within HR, your security groups might need a manual refresh. Log out of Workday entirely and log back in.
3. For report generation errors, verify that you are selecting a supervisory organization you are authorized to view.
4. If access is still missing, escalate to the HRIS (HR Information Systems) team by opening a ticket with the exact error code.

Affected Systems: Workday
Category: Software / HR

title: Salesforce Single Sign-On (SSO) Error
content:
Problem: Sales representative cannot log into Salesforce via Okta/SSO.

Symptoms:
- Okta dashboard throws 'App Not Assigned' when clicking Salesforce
- Salesforce shows 'SAML Error: Invalid Issuer' after Okta redirect
- Account locked in Salesforce

Resolution Steps:
1. If Okta shows 'App Not Assigned', your Salesforce license has not been provisioned yet. Request access via the IT Portal.
2. If you see 'SAML Error', clear your browser cookies for both salesforce.com and okta.com, then restart the browser.
3. If your account is locked in Salesforce, wait 15 minutes for the auto-unlock to trigger, then try again.
4. Ensure you are not trying to log into a sandbox environment using production SSO credentials, as sandboxes often have different SSO setups.
5. If issues persist, raise a ticket specifying 'Salesforce SSO Issue'.

Affected Systems: Salesforce, Okta
Category: Access / SSO

title: Adobe Creative Cloud License Deactivated
content:
Problem: Marketing user's Adobe CC suite apps (Photoshop, Illustrator) show as 'Trial Expired' or 'License Required'.

Symptoms:
- Apps open but prompt for payment
- Creative Cloud desktop app shows 'Sign in to activate'
- User is signed in but gets a 'Subscription not found' error

Resolution Steps:
1. Open the Adobe Creative Cloud desktop app.
2. Click your profile icon > Sign Out.
3. Click 'Sign in with your Enterprise ID' or 'Company or School Account' (do not use a personal Adobe ID).
4. Authenticate using corporate SSO.
5. If the app still says no subscription, check the IT portal to ensure your Adobe CC request has been approved by the Marketing Director.
6. If approved but failing, your license might be assigned to a different Adobe tenant. Open an IT ticket to sync the Adobe Admin Console.

Affected Systems: Adobe Creative Cloud
Category: Software / Licenses
